hobbies that will make you
dangerously informed

reading one long article

read one long article a day from start to finish instead of fifty headlines. knowing one story well beats knowing a thousand titles, and people can always tell the difference.

following the money

when you hear a big story, ask yourself who pays for it and who profits from it. this one question helps you see through half the news before anyone else around you does.

a daily lesson

spend 5 minutes a day on one lesson in something you never studied: economics, art history, how the brain works. small daily lessons add up to the kind of knowledge people notice.
slides.texte_sophia:
a daily lesson

i spend 5 minutes a day on one lesson in something i never studied: economics, art history. i do it with the Sophia app, one lesson a day, and people notice what i know now.

slides.texte_overlay:
old newspapers

once a week, read a newspaper from fifty years ago online. seeing what people worried about back then makes you calmer, and sharper, about what everyone worries about today.

asking experts

ask one person a week to explain their job to you like you know nothing. everyone is an expert in something, and most people are thrilled when someone finally asks them.
